title: Warrior Song of Tirot Sing's Freedom Fighters (Rwai Shlur Ki Khla-Wait)
khasi_title: Rwai Shlur Ki Khla-Wait U Tirot Sing
cultural_context: The rousing battle chant sung by the warriors (Khla-Wait) of Nongkhlaw before the march to defend the Khasi Hills, from Victor G. Bareh's classic play 'Ka Drama U Tirot Sing'.

khasi: Ieng, ko khla-wait jong ka ri,
Bat la ka waitlam ba shlur;
U Tirot Sing u ialam shaphrang,
Ban iada ia ka ri bad ka khet;
Wat rieh, wat shepteng hakhmat ka thma,
Kham bha ban iap kum u rangbah,
Ban ia kaba shong kum u mraw
Ha la ka ri ba la buh u Blei.
english: Arise, O valiant warriors of our motherland,
To defend our land and royal throne;
Flinch not, dread not before the clash of war,
Far nobler to die as a free man,
Than to live as a subjugated slave
In our native land ordained by God.

khasi: Ki lum ki wah kin phla ia ka hok,
Ka snam jong ngi kan pynim ia ka ri;
Naduh Nongkhlaw haduh Sohra ba phriang,
Ka sur jong ka jinglaitluid kan sawa;
U Syiem u ieng ha ka nia ba skhem,
Ha khmat u Nongthaw ngin aiti la ka met,
Ban pynsah ia ka burom ka jaidbynriew.
english: The crags and rivers shall bear witness to our cause,
Our blood shall water the liberty of the land;
From Nongkhlaw unto the heights of Sohra,
The roar of freedom shall echo forth;
Our King stands on unwavering truth,
The Seven Huts shall never bow the knee;
Before the Creator we offer up our mortal lives,
To preserve the immortal honor of our people.

vocabulary.khla-wait: warrior / knight / tiger of the sword
vocabulary.tirot sing: U Tirot Sing Syiem (national hero of Khasi independence)
